# The North Star That Never Moves

## Scripture

"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit." — Psalm 147:4–5 (NIV)

## Reflection

On a clear October night, find the Big Dipper and follow its pointer stars to Polaris—the North Star. While the entire sky wheels slowly overhead through the night, Polaris stays fixed. Sailors, shepherds, and travelers have steered by it for centuries. But here's the wonder: Polaris isn't motionless because it's special in itself. It simply sits almost directly above Earth's axis, so as our planet turns, the star appears to stand still while everything else circles around it.

Our lives are like the rest of that sky—turning, shifting, seasons changing, circumstances spinning in ways we didn't plan. Yet God's Word tells us He numbers the stars and calls each one by name. The same voice that fixed the heavens in their courses holds your days in His understanding, which has no limit.

Maybe tonight you feel like the sky around you is in motion and nothing is steady. Look north. The star that anchors the night sky is a small reminder of a much greater anchor: the God who named every star knows your name too. He is not tossed about by the turning of your seasons. He is the fixed point around which everything truly revolves.

## Prayer

Lord of the heavens, You call every star by name—and You know mine. When my world spins and seasons shift, fix my heart on You, the unchanging anchor of my soul. Thank You that Your understanding has no limit and Your care never drifts. Help me to look up with trust tonight. In Jesus' name, amen.
